strongest_objection: Big holder wants the high price, the map's near priority and the target of two edges, states an arithmetic that is wrong on its face: an investor's interest in the round price does not have the sign of its existing stake's value minus its new dollars. Ownership after the round is (old fraction times pre-money plus new dollars) over post-money, whose derivative in price has the sign of pro-rata share of the round minus new dollars. A full pro-rata participant is price-indifferent in ownership, a sub-pro-rata holder wants the price up, a super-pro-rata holder wants it down, and the letter separately rewards every old share at the new price. The author's rule, applied as the near priority's test instructs, predicts that nearly every insider argues up, since stake value usually exceeds new money, and would miss the small holder funding a bridge. The behavior the item names survives and the two edges into it get cleaner under the corrected sign (at the concentration cap the new dollars are zero, so the capped fund is the purest price hawk), which is why this is a repair and not a return. Second in weight: Fund that grew away hides that the grown fund could lead by ballooning the round, so its silence is really Fund on one exit rerun with a denominator fees enlarged; naming that makes it the mirror of Living dead by denominator and strengthens the map's own hinge.

items.item: Table below the line: a round made only of checks that sit below each writer's own care line has no holder whose arithmetic makes it show up at the bridge, so the party round of twelve small checks is cheap and quick to raise and nobody's when the company needs a lead, a bridge, or a signature in a hurry; the carrier is the sum of ratios across the table rather than any one of them, the behavior is a cap table that goes silent at once, and the founder's move is to seat at least one holder for whom the position is large relative to its fund, even at a worse price, since that holder will do the work; not Below the care line, which is one indifferent check, since twelve indifferent checks make a second thing, a table with no seat, and it vanishes the moment any one check crosses its writer's line.
items.why: The carrier is stated as the sum of check-to-fund ratios, but the item's own closing clause says the table wakes the moment any one check crosses its writer's line, which is a condition on the largest ratio, not the sum; twelve tiny ratios can sum past a threshold that no holder individually meets and the table stays silent.
items.repair: Table below the line: a round made only of checks that sit below each writer's own care line has no holder whose arithmetic makes it show up at the bridge, so the party round of twelve small checks is cheap and quick to raise and nobody's when the company needs a lead, a bridge, or a signature in a hurry; the carrier is the largest check-to-fund ratio on the table rather than any one check, since the table is silent only while every ratio sits below its writer's line, the behavior is a cap table that goes silent at once, and the founder's move is to seat at least one holder for whom the position is large relative to its fund, even at a worse price, since that holder will do the work; not Below the care line, which is one indifferent check, since twelve indifferent checks make a second thing, a table with no seat, and it vanishes the moment any one check crosses its writer's line.

items.item: Fund that grew away: management fees are a percentage of committed capital, so the partners' income doubles when the fund does, and the successor fund is sized by what the limited partners will give and what the fees need rather than by what the portfolio will need, so the fund that led the seed at fifty million has raised five hundred by the A and can no longer write a check the A can absorb at its ownership target; the carrier is the fee on committed capital, the behavior is the insider who cheers the company and cannot lead its next round, which then reads as the silence above, and the founder's move is to ask which fund the pro-rata will be drawn from and to read the insider's own fundraising as a forecast of who will be at the next table; contested as a critique of managers, kept here as arithmetic about which fund exists when the next round comes; not Below the care line, since this fund was the right size when it arrived and moved.
items.why: As written, the grown fund 'cannot write a check the A can absorb', but Round sized from the far end on the same map says such a fund resizes the round to its check. So the grown fund's absence is not an impossibility but a refusal: the company that passed the fund-returner test at fifty million fails it at five hundred. The mechanism is Fund on one exit rerun on an existing position because fees moved the denominator, and the map already has the downward version (Living dead by denominator, secondary to a smaller fund). Saying so keeps the fee arithmetic, corrects the behavior claim, and gives the founder a computable pre-test instead of only a forecast.
items.repair: Fund that grew away: management fees are a percentage of committed capital, so the partners' income doubles when the fund does, and the successor fund is sized by what the limited partners will give and what the fees need rather than by what the portfolio will need, so the fund that led the seed at fifty million has raised five hundred by the A, and the company is run through Fund on one exit a second time with a denominator ten times larger, which the company that returned fifty million at ten percent no longer passes; the grown fund could still lead by resizing the round to its check, as in Round sized from the far end, so its refusal is the failed test and the check the A cannot absorb is the symptom; the carrier is the fee on committed capital, the behavior is the insider who cheers the company and will not lead its next round at either size, which then reads as the silence above, and the founder's move is to ask which fund the pro-rata will be drawn from, to read the insider's own fundraising as a forecast of who will be at the next table, and to rerun the fund-returner test against the successor's size before counting on the insider; contested as a critique of managers, kept here as arithmetic about which fund exists when the next round comes; not Below the care line, since this fund was the right size when it arrived and moved, and the mirror of Living dead by denominator, where the denominator shrinks by secondary instead of growing by fees.

items.item: Big holder wants the high price: on a round it partly funds, an investor's stake in the price has the sign of its existing position's value minus its new dollars, so a holder with twenty percent worth twenty million that puts four million into the round gains more on the letter from a higher price than it pays in the round and argues the price up, while the two-percent holder and the new lead argue it down; the carrier is the ratio of stake to new money, the behavior is the largest insider taking the founder's side on price at the bridge, and the founder's move is to read each holder's stance on price off the cap table before the meeting rather than off its faith in the company, and to let the big holder name the number the new money must meet; not generosity, and reversed the moment the round is large relative to the stake, as at a recapitalization, where the same holder wants the price down.
items.why: The sign rule is wrong; see strongest objection. The corrected rule keeps the strange claim (largest insider as the founder's ally on price) and the reversal at a recapitalization, and separates the letter effect (every old share marks up regardless of new money) from the ownership effect (sign of pro-rata minus new dollars). The near priority's next_question should compute pro-rata share of the round minus new dollars, not stake value minus new dollars, or its miss count will be meaningless.
items.repair: Big holder wants the high price: on a round it partly funds, an investor's stake in the price has the sign of its pro-rata share of the round minus its new dollars, since its ownership after the round is its old shares plus its new money over the post-money, and that fraction rises with the price exactly when the new money is below pro-rata, so a holder with twenty percent that puts two million into a twenty-million-dollar round, where its pro-rata is four, argues the price up, a two-percent holder putting in the same two million argues it down, and the new lead, with no old shares, argues it down hardest, while a holder taking exactly its pro-rata is indifferent in ownership and argues up only for the letter, which marks every old share at the new price whatever the holder paid for the new ones; the carrier is the ratio of new money to pro-rata, the behavior is the largest insider taking the founder's side on price at the bridge, and the founder's move is to read each holder's stance on price off the cap table and the round size before the meeting rather than off its faith in the company, and to let the big holder name the number the new money must meet; not generosity, and reversed the moment the holder's new money exceeds its pro-rata, as at a recapitalization it funds alone, where the same holder wants the price down.

items.item: Vintage's two appetites: a fund raises its successor on its marks two to four years in and on its distributions after, and is wound up at ten years plus extensions, so a young fund wants a priced up-round before its next raise and an old fund wants cash, and the same company hears 'raise more, go bigger' from one board seat and 'take the offer' from the other, each seat reading its own fund's calendar, as the whaling agent wanted the ship home with the oil while the captain wanted one more whale; the carrier is the term in the limited partnership agreement and the fundraising it forces, the behavior is a board split by vintage rather than by belief, and the founder's move is to read each investor's stance on the fork from its fund's age before asking, and to seat funds whose calendars agree; not tollgates-that-must-buy's Powder that must be lit, which is the compulsion to buy by a date, since this is what the fund needs to have happened to your company by when, and Sequoia's 2021 restructuring of its US and European business into an open-ended fund without a term removed exactly this behavior and no other on the map.
items.why: The Sequoia 2021 restructuring is documented, but 'removed exactly this behavior and no other on the map' is an illustrative case asserted as a precise fact. An open-ended vehicle removes the term and intensifies the letter items, since its mark becomes the price at which limited partners redeem, and its sub-funds still carry carry. The record's own boundary claim concedes the far pole is really 'closed-end fund with a quarterly letter'; the item should not claim more than the boundary does.
items.repair: Vintage's two appetites: a fund raises its successor on its marks two to four years in and on its distributions after, and is wound up at ten years plus extensions, so a young fund wants a priced up-round before its next raise and an old fund wants cash, and the same company hears 'raise more, go bigger' from one board seat and 'take the offer' from the other, each seat reading its own fund's calendar, as the whaling agent wanted the ship home with the oil while the captain wanted one more whale; the carrier is the term in the limited partnership agreement and the fundraising it forces, the behavior is a board split by vintage rather than by belief, and the founder's move is to read each investor's stance on the fork from its fund's age before asking, and to seat funds whose calendars agree; not tollgates-that-must-buy's Powder that must be lit, which is the compulsion to buy by a date, since this is what the fund needs to have happened to your company by when, and Sequoia's 2021 restructuring of its US and European business into an open-ended fund without a term removed the term and with it this behavior, while sharpening the letter items, since an open-ended fund's mark is also the price at which its limited partners may leave.

items.item: Call option at the board: carry is a share of profit above capital returned, a call option on the whole fund, so a fund whose portfolio is under water holds an option out of the money and wants variance, opposing the sale at one times that would return capital and pressing for the raise that might return the fund, while a fund already returned wants to lock in and supports the sale; the carrier is the moneyness of the carry, the behavior is a board seat's stance on the acquisition offer set by the rest of that fund's portfolio, which the founder never sees, and the founder's move is to ask how the fund is doing before asking what it thinks, and to expect the under-water fund to want the swing that a diversified holder would not; by analogy the whaling captain on a lay with an empty hold late in the voyage hunts the worse water; not Fund on one exit, which is applied at entry to a company, since this is applied at exit by a portfolio's state, and it does not move when the fund is halved.
items.why: My boundary case (the preferred return) shows 'a fund already returned' is not where the option is in the money: under an eight-percent hurdle compounding seven years the strike is about 1.7 times capital, so a fund at one and a half times still holds an out-of-the-money option and still wants variance. Many US venture agreements carry no hurdle, so the clause is conditioned on the agreement; the mechanism is unchanged, the strike is named.
items.repair: Call option at the board: carry is a share of profit above capital returned, a call option on the whole fund, so a fund whose portfolio is under water holds an option out of the money and wants variance, opposing the sale at one times that would return capital and pressing for the raise that might return the fund, while a fund already past its strike wants to lock in and supports the sale, and where the agreement carries a preferred return the strike sits above capital, so a fund at one and a half times in its seventh year under an eight-percent hurdle is still out of the money and still wants the swing; the carrier is the moneyness of the carry, the behavior is a board seat's stance on the acquisition offer set by the rest of that fund's portfolio, which the founder never sees, and the founder's move is to ask how the fund is doing before asking what it thinks, and to expect the under-water fund to want the swing that a diversified holder would not; by analogy the whaling captain on a lay with an empty hold late in the voyage hunts the worse water; not Fund on one exit, which is applied at entry to a company, since this is applied at exit by a portfolio's state, and it does not move when the fund is halved.

items.item: Orphan on the board: carry is divided among partners by attribution, and a partner's standing rides on the deals carried under their name inside their own promotion window, so a junior partner wants a visible markup by a brand-name lead before the partnership vote and will help the founder get one at a lower ownership, and when a partner leaves the company loses the one person in the reserve model whose carry it was, so the successor, who gets no credit for it, lets it drift into the living dead regardless of its numbers; the carrier is the attribution of carry and the partner's clock inside the fund's, the behavior is a company whose treatment changes on a personnel move nobody at the company made, and the founder's move is to negotiate a named successor with attribution on departure, or to buy the position out; adjacent to deal-deaths' Champion's single-tender want, which kills a deal before signing, since this changes the treatment of a company already owned.
items.why: The item carries two behaviors under one carrier: the junior partner who wants a brand-name markup inside a promotion window, and the orphan left when a partner departs. The type requires a founder-side move per behavior and only the orphan has one. Rather than cut the promotion-window half, which is a real and usable clock, the repair gives it its move.
items.repair: Orphan on the board: carry is divided among partners by attribution, and a partner's standing rides on the deals carried under their name inside their own promotion window, so a junior partner wants a visible markup by a brand-name lead before the partnership vote and will help the founder get one at a lower ownership, and when a partner leaves the company loses the one person in the reserve model whose carry it was, so the successor, who gets no credit for it, lets it drift into the living dead regardless of its numbers; the carrier is the attribution of carry and the partner's clock inside the fund's, the behavior is a company whose treatment changes on a personnel move nobody at the company made, and the founder's move is, on the way up, to time the A to the sponsor's promotion window and let the sponsor's need for a brand-name markup pay for the ownership the fund would otherwise hold out for, and, on departure, to negotiate a named successor with attribution, or to buy the position out; adjacent to deal-deaths' Champion's single-tender want, which kills a deal before signing, since this changes the treatment of a company already owned.

items.item: Silence of the one who could have: when a fund large enough to lead the next round takes a small position in this one, its later absence from the round is read by every outsider as knowledge, since the party with the most information and the most money declined, so the seed from the big fund carries a signal at the A that the same seed from a fund that never leads As cannot carry; the carrier is the insider's capacity relative to the round, the behavior is the outsider's question 'why isn't your seed investor leading', which the insider cannot answer without either leading or damning, and the founder's move is to take seed from funds too small to lead, or from a program the big fund has walled off by policy so that its silence is a rule rather than a verdict; not Pockets, not opinion, where the absence is arithmetic, since this absence is a choice, and the signal exists only where the fund is big enough to have had one.
items.why: Tested as the right-hand neighbor against Fund that grew away (see neighbor_test); separable by whether the absence is computable from public numbers before the fund speaks.

items.item: Mark kept by structure: a fund's mark is made on the headline price and not on the preference-adjusted value, so a fund facing a down round prefers a flat price with a senior preference, a multiple, or a ratchet to a lower price with clean terms, because the letter records the price and the structure is invisible to it, and the founder's ownership drains through the preference stack at a price that never moved; the carrier is a valuation policy that reads price and not terms, the behavior is 'we can hold the valuation if we add some protection', and the founder's move is to price the structure as the down round it is, to take the clean lower price when the common's share of the plausible exits is higher under it, and to hear the insider's preference for structure as a statement about its letter and not about the company; adds to dilution-carriers' Headline bought with terms, which prices the trade, the investor's motive for it, a letter that cannot see the terms; not the preference itself, which is a term, and present at any fund size, since the letter is written for whoever's money it is.
items.why: Kept, with a modality note: 'a fund's mark is made on the headline price and not on the preference-adjusted value' is true of policies that read the headline and false of policies that backsolve an option-pricing waterfall, which auditors increasingly require. The item's own carrier clause ('a valuation policy that reads price and not terms') already scopes it, so no text change; the record's mode field should not read it as universal.

neighbor_test.left: Fund that grew away: management fees are a percentage of committed capital, so the partners' income doubles when the fund does, and the successor fund is sized by what the limited partners will give and what the fees need rather than by what the portfolio will need, so the fund that led the seed at fifty million has raised five hundred by the A and can no longer write a check the A can absorb at its ownership target; the carrier is the fee on committed capital, the behavior is the insider who cheers the company and cannot lead its next round, which then reads as the silence above, and the founder's move is to ask which fund the pro-rata will be drawn from and to read the insider's own fundraising as a forecast of who will be at the next table; contested as a critique of managers, kept here as arithmetic about which fund exists when the next round comes; not Below the care line, since this fund was the right size when it arrived and moved.
neighbor_test.right: Silence of the one who could have: when a fund large enough to lead the next round takes a small position in this one, its later absence from the round is read by every outsider as knowledge, since the party with the most information and the most money declined, so the seed from the big fund carries a signal at the A that the same seed from a fund that never leads As cannot carry; the carrier is the insider's capacity relative to the round, the behavior is the outsider's question 'why isn't your seed investor leading', which the insider cannot answer without either leading or damning, and the founder's move is to take seed from funds too small to lead, or from a program the big fund has walled off by policy so that its silence is a rule rather than a verdict; not Pockets, not opinion, where the absence is arithmetic, since this absence is a choice, and the signal exists only where the fund is big enough to have had one.
neighbor_test.separating_case: Both produce the same observable, an insider that took the seed and is absent at the A, and the author's own text concedes one 'reads as the silence above', so this is the pair nearest collapse, nearer than the author's Silence/Pockets pair. Separating case: the founder offers the insider the lead at the insider's current check and ownership target, ignoring the company's plan. The grown fund whose successor is ten times its seed-era fund answers from arithmetic the founder can compute in advance (successor size over ownership target against the plausible exit): a yes balloons the round as in Round sized from the far end, a no was predictable from the successor's announced size, and the founder can pre-empt outsiders with the number. The fund whose silence is a verdict gives a no at every round size that no public figure predicts. One absence is computable from the insider's own fundraising before the insider speaks; the other is not, and only the second carries information about the company. They separate, and the repair to Fund that grew away is what makes the separation explicit.

boundary_case: The preferred return (an eight-percent hurdle before carry) is my tempting nonmember: it is fund arithmetic, it is other people's money, and it visibly changes what a board seat wants. Ruling: out as an item, in as a parameter, because it produces no behavior of its own; it moves the strike of the call option in Call option at the board, so that a fund which has returned capital is still out of the money. The ruling forced the repair to that item. A second candidate, the partner's own leveraged commitment to the fund (a general-partner commit financed by a loan, producing an appetite for early distributions), is a plausible member the map does not contain; it is the partner's money rather than other people's, so it would sit oddly on the far pole, and I leave it as a note rather than an admission.

seriation.note: The endpoints are real: Below the care line vanishes outright on resizing and Vote without a checkbook is what remains at size zero. The consequential adjacency Pockets, not opinion → Vote without a checkbook teaches: the same absence is a curable ledger fact about one company on one side and a standing veto about the whole fund on the other, and the founder's move changes kind. Big holder's placement as the first size-invariant behavior survives the corrected arithmetic, since pro-rata minus new money scales with the fund and keeps its sign under proportional halving. One honesty note: the second half is a grouping by carrier (letter, term, carry, cap, ledger, agreement), not a gradient; the author says itinerary and it is one, but no direction runs through the grouping, so adjacencies inside it (letter → term, carry → cap) teach less than the two the note defends.

edges.to_handle: Big holder wants the high price
edges.why: Under the corrected arithmetic the big holder's preference for a high price has an ownership component that exists whether or not a stranger signs; only the letter component waits for the outsider. 'Earns nothing' is true of the letter and false of the ownership, and the dependency the edge draws is on the letter half.
edges.repair_label: If the fund's valuation policy discounts a price no outsider set, then the big holder's preference for a high price earns nothing on the letter until a stranger signs at it, and only the ownership arithmetic remains, so the holder who argues the founder's side on price must also recruit the one party that argues against it.

edges.to_handle: Big holder wants the high price
edges.why: Tested against the corrected sign: at the cap the fund's new dollars are zero, so pro-rata minus new money is maximal and the capped fund is the purest price hawk on the round it must yield. The incompatibility (mark or ownership, not both) is sharper after the repair, not weaker.

modality_problems: Big holder wants the high price: the sign rule 'existing position's value minus new dollars' is asserted as arithmetic and is not; the correct sign is pro-rata share of the round minus new dollars, with the letter as a separate always-positive term.
Table below the line: 'sum of ratios' is asserted where the item's own logic uses the largest ratio.

Vintage's two appetites: the Sequoia 2021 case is documented but 'removed exactly this behavior and no other on the map' overclaims; an evergreen intensifies the letter items and keeps carry at the sub-fund level.
Fund that grew away: 'can no longer write a check the A can absorb' presents a refusal as an impossibility; the same map's Round sized from the far end shows the fund could resize the round.
Call option at the board: 'already returned' as the in-the-money boundary ignores the preferred return where the agreement carries one.

Mark kept by structure: 'a fund's mark is made on the headline price' is scoped by its carrier clause but reads as universal; option-pricing backsolves that see the preference stack are common under fair-value audits.
Stranger's price on the letter: an insider-only round 'marks little' in the mechanism and 'marks nothing' in the discriminator; the first is right.

The whaling agent versus captain analogy is flagged as analogy and used twice; acceptable, though under the lay system captain and owner both wanted a full ship and the divergence was on time and risk, which is the point the item wants, so no change.
duplication: None in ideonomy/data/grown.jsonl. Borders two siblings in this run: investor-tells' Next-round hand reads the same absence at the next round that this map explains from four causes (Silence, Fund that grew away, Cap, Pockets), which is complementary rather than duplicate and worth a cross-reference the record does not yet make; term-sheet-powers' reserve items and dilution-carriers' Headline bought with terms and Veto without votes are cited with what each item adds, and the additions hold.
best_unresolved_seed: The mark that is also the exit: in an open-ended vehicle the quarterly letter stops being a report and becomes the price at which the other people leave, so the two letter items (Stranger's price on the letter, Mark kept by structure) acquire a redemption clock the closed-end fund never had, and a new behavior appears that the map's Sequoia clause points at but does not contain, the evergreen that must procure a stranger's mark-up to stop its own limited partners redeeming. Sorting the far half by which vehicle change removes or intensifies each item, as the author's own next opening proposes, would find it.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing the price-stance arithmetic in Big holder wants the high price and its dependent edge, restating Fund that grew away as the fund-returner test rerun with a fee-grown denominator, correcting the carrier of Table below the line, scoping the Sequoia claim, naming the carry's strike under a hurdle, and giving Orphan on the board's promotion-window half its founder move.
